arxiv-2205-06226.title: The Mechanism of Prediction Head in Non-contrastive Self-supervised Learning
arxiv-2205-06226.creator: Zixin Wen, Yuanzhi Li
arxiv-2205-06226.description: Abstract Recently the surprising discovery of Bootstrap Your Own Latent ( BYOL ) method by Grill et al. 2020 shows the negative term in contrastive loss can be removed if we add the so-called prediction head to the network architecture, which breaks the symmetry between the positive pairs. This initiated the research of non-contrastive self-supervised learning .

arxiv-2404-02614.title: Vestibular schwannoma growth prediction from longitudinal MRI by time-conditioned neural fields
arxiv-2404-02614.creator: Yunjie Chen, Jelmer M. Wolterink, Olaf M. Neve, Stephan R. Romeijn, Berit M. Verbist, Erik F. Hensen, Qian Tao, Marius Staring
arxiv-2404-02614.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yunjie Chen, Jelmer M. Wolterink, Olaf M. Neve, Stephan R. Romeijn, Berit M. Verbist, Erik F. Hensen, Qian Tao, Marius Staring. Vestibular schwannomas (VS) are benign tumors that are generally managed by active surveillance with MRI examination. To further assist clinical decision-making and avoid overtreatment, an accurate prediction of tumor growth based on longitudinal imaging is highly desirable. In this paper, we introduce DeepGrowth, a deep learning method that incorporates neural fields and recurrent neural networks for prospective tumor growth prediction.

arxiv-2511-21706.title: A General Highly Accurate Online Planning Method Integrating Large Language Models into Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation for Dialogue Tasks
arxiv-2511-21706.creator: Hui Wang, Fafa Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Chaoxu Mu
arxiv-2511-21706.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hui Wang, Fafa Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Chaoxu Mu. In goal-oriented dialogue tasks, the main challenge is to steer the interaction towards a given goal within a limited number of turns. Existing approaches either rely on elaborate prompt engineering, whose effectiveness is heavily dependent on human experience, or integrate policy networks and pre-trained policy models, which are usually difficult to adapt to new dialogue scenarios and costly to train.

arxiv-2512-14644.title: Attention-Based Preprocessing Framework for Improving Rare Transient Classification
arxiv-2512-14644.creator: Xinyue Sheng, Tuan Dung Pham, Zichi Zhang, Matt Nicholl, Thai Son Mai
arxiv-2512-14644.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xinyue Sheng, Tuan Dung Pham, Zichi Zhang, Matt Nicholl, Thai Son Mai. With large numbers of transients discovered by current and future imaging surveys, machine learning is increasingly applied to light curve and host galaxy properties to select events for follow-up. However, finding rare types of transients remains difficult due to extreme class imbalances in training sets, and extracting features from host images is complicated by the presence of bright foreground sources, particularly if the true host is faint or distant.

arxiv-2602-08946.title: Coulomb corrections for the non-flip and spin-flip electromagnetic 𝒑 ↑ ​ 𝑨 \boldsymbol{p}^{\uparrow}\!\boldsymbol{A} amplitudes
arxiv-2602-08946.creator: A. A. Poblaguev
arxiv-2602-08946.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by A. A. Poblaguev. It is demonstrated that, within the eikonal approach, the Coulomb corrections to the elastic electromagnetic non-flip and spin-flip proton–nucleus amplitudes are identical when the two amplitudes share the same exponential form factors. This result allows Coulomb corrections to be computed numerically, and with high precision, for both electromagnetic and hadronic elastic p ↑ ​ A p^{\uparrow}A amplitudes in the massless-photon limit, including the effects of soft magnetic photon exchange.

pmc-11517481.title: Sick-leave trajectories among people sickness absent with stress-related diagnoses; cohort studies
pmc-11517481.creator: K Gemes, E Petterson, K Farrants, E Friberg, K Nilsson, S Sjölund Andoff, K Alexanderson
pmc-11517481.description: BackgroundStress-related disorders are common sickness absence (SA) diagnoses in many Western countries. Knowledge of SA and disability pension (DP) patterns among people with such SA is needed. Thus, the aim was to identify future SADP trajectories among people with a new SA spell due to stress-related diagnosis and to examine sociodemographic and health-related factors associated with identified trajectories.

pmc-11557463.title: The influence of family socioeconomic status on college students’ mental health literacy: the chain mediating effect of parenting styles and interpersonal relationships
pmc-11557463.creator: Jie Wu, Haoyuan Shen, Yunbo Shen, Xianglin Liao, Xianglian Yu
pmc-11557463.description: IntroductionWith the increasing prevalence of mental health challenges among college students, understanding how family background and interpersonal dynamics affect mental health literacy is critical. This study examined the relationships between family socioeconomic status, mental health literacy, parenting styles, and interpersonal relationships among 1,107 college students.

pmc-12630336.title: Genetic diversity and population structure of sour passion fruit in Brazil
pmc-12630336.creator: Carolina Sampaio Araponga, Gonçalo Santos Silva, Cláusio Antônio Ferreira de Melo, Margarete Magalhães Souza
pmc-12630336.description: Highlights•ISSR markers revealed high intraspecific polymorphism in Passiflora edulis populations.•Five populations were identified among analyzed accessions.•Most molecular variance (55%) was detected within rather than between populations.•Field-collected populations showed greater diversity than commercial seed sources.•Results support the strategic use of genetic structure for passion fruit breeding.

pmc-12744897.title: Geometric‐Mean Fitness Does Not Correspond to Long‐Term Survival Probability
pmc-12744897.creator: Takuya Okabe, Jin Yoshimura, Hiromu Ito
pmc-12744897.description: Unpredictable randomness plays a crucial role in long‐term sustainability of biological systems. The population growth of a species in variable environments is typically described in terms of a long‐term measure like geometric‐mean fitness, or geometric mean of stochastic growth rates.

pmc-13238940.title: Anti-CD19-engineered exosomes enable B cell-targeted anti-BAFF mRNA delivery to alleviate lupus progression
pmc-13238940.creator: Linda Zeng, Jingxian Shu, Shuping Zhong, Xin Dong, Yongjian Wu, Xi Huang
pmc-13238940.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease characterized by abnormal activation of B cells. Excessive B cell activating factor (BAFF) of the tumor necrosis factor family plays an essential role in B cell hyperactivation. Blocking the binding of excessive BAFF to its receptors is becoming a promising approach for SLE treatment.

pmc-13246989.title: Predictive value of inferior mesenteric artery size in type 2 endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair—a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13246989.creator: Galaleldin Abdelhalim, Chris Grieco, Oliver Chan, Hariesha Pathmaraj, Lexy Sorrell, Katie Carpenter, Paul Jenkins
pmc-13246989.description: BackgroundType II endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair is the most common endoleak type. Identifying pre-operative anatomical features that could signal higher risk will improve surveillance post-procedure. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) diameter and type II endoleak.

pmc-13269128.title: The global burden of mental and substance use disorders among adolescents and young adults
pmc-13269128.creator: Xiangyu Zhao, Ligang Liu, Luofei Zhang, Pujing Zhao, Wenshuo Jiang, Milap C Nahata
pmc-13269128.description: Mental disorders and substance use disorders (SUDs) are significant public health challenges among adolescents and young adults (AYAs). This study quantified global and regional prevalence, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and years lived with disability (YLDs), and temporal trends of mental disorders and SUDs among AYAs from 1990–2021. Estimates were generated using DisMod-MR 2.

pmc-13298252.title: Functional Characteristics of Walnut Protein Fractions and Rutin Loading by Albumin
pmc-13298252.creator: Yue Wang, Xiang Li, Yu Zhou, Zilin Wang, Yuanli Wang, Fengyating Wu, Yang Tian, Liang Tao
pmc-13298252.description: This study aimed to systematically compare the functional properties of the four major components (albumin, globulin, prolamin, and glutelin) of protein from Yunnan deep-veined walnuts to screen for protein-based carrier materials with good processing adaptability and the ability to efficiently encapsulate the active ingredient rutin. In addition, the binding and molecular interactions between the preferred protein and rutin were analyzed.

pmc-13450917.title: New insights in submucous fibrosis: Nicotine dependence and nutritional assessment
pmc-13450917.creator: Rishabh Sachdeva, Aadithya B. Urs, Priya Kumar, Bhawna Mahajan
pmc-13450917.description: Background:Submucous fibrosis (SMF) is an oral potentially malignant disorder with a high risk of malignant transformation, primarily associated with areca nut use and tobacco consumption.Aim:This study aimed to evaluate the correlation of nicotine dependence and nutritional status with disease severity in patients with SMF.Settings and Design:This observational study was conducted among 70 SMF patients subdivided on clinical and histological classification.
